title: Tamsin and the Bakery
premise: Emrys Dravenmoor left her coastal hometown eleven years ago after a betrayal she never named, building a careful life counting sea turtles and keeping her heart 'trained' against attachment. When her aunt dies and leaves her the failing Tamsin and the Bakery—a vineyard-adjacent café run by Tamsin Vale, the woman whose letter Emrys never answered—Emrys returns intending to sell and vanish again. But the lost letter resurfaces, forcing both women to confront what justice looks like when the law protected the wrong person back then: the vineyard owner who ruined Tamsin's family still holds power over the town. As harvest approaches, Emrys must choose between her invisible, containable life and staying past the last train—fighting for Tamsin, the bakery, and a reckoning the courts never delivered.
about_author: Gideon Yarrow is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent a decade covering coastal communities and the quiet injustices they harbor. They write romances where love is an act of courage rather than an accident.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. On a research vessel, Emrys catalogs nesting turtles with methodical detachment, insisting to a colleague that hearts are trainable muscles. A solicitor's letter arrives: her Aunt Wren has died, leaving her half of 'Tamsin and the Bakery.' The emotional beat is controlled grief cracking into dread—she knows exactly which town that name points to.

chapters.title: The Last Train Platform
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys arrives in Harrow Vale intending a forty-eight-hour visit: appraise the property, sign papers, leave. She encounters Tamsin Vale flour-dusted and furious, who assumed Wren would never sell. Their old wound surfaces immediately, unspoken. Beat: hostile recognition, two people armored in competence.

chapters.title: Flour and Salt
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Tamsin narrates the bakery's daily rhythm and her precarious lease with Corwin Ashe, the vineyard magnate whose family destroyed hers years ago. She needs Wren's half to survive; Emrys's arrival threatens everything. Forced proximity begins when Emrys misses her return train. Beat: reluctant truce sealed over bread at midnight.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Sorting Wren's attic, Emrys finds her own unsent reply to Tamsin—written at seventeen, hidden by Wren to protect her from Ashe's retaliation. Reading her younger self's words, Emrys confronts why she fled: she witnessed something about Ashe she was paid to forget. Beat: shame and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Harvest Terms
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Ashe offers Tamsin a new lease with predatory terms unless she sells outright. Emrys unexpectedly negotiates on her behalf, revealing a sharp legal mind Tamsin never knew. They begin digging into the old case together. Beat: alliance forming, attraction admitted only through argument.

chapters.title: The Vineyard's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Following Wren's records, Emrys discovers her aunt quietly documented Ashe's fraud for years—the same corruption Emrys witnessed at seventeen. Staying invisible starts to feel like complicity. A first kiss happens in the bakery's cold store, immediately regretted. Beat: desire versus self-protection.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Proofing Room
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. The bakery is vandalized; Ashe denies involvement but the message is clear. Tamsin wants to fight; Emrys, terrified of repeating history, urges flight and offers to buy her out generously. Their worst fight yet. Beat: the price of survival made literal—safety offered as abandonment.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys tracks down the town clerk and a retired deputy willing to speak, assembling Wren's evidence into something usable outside the courts that failed them before. She chooses visibility: her name, her testimony, her history with Ashe exposed. Beat: courage replacing containment.

chapters.title: The Night Before Harvest
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. On harvest eve, the evidence goes public—town meeting, Ashe confronted, his creditors and partners abandoning him. But victory costs Emrys a job offer abroad and her carefully built anonymity. At the last train, Tamsin doesn't beg; she simply leaves the bakery light on. Beat: climax and surrender to hope.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: POV Both, alternating. Weeks later, the bakery thrives on festival traffic from the freed vineyard; Emrys has stayed, teaching marine science at the local school and kneading dough badly at dawn. Together they hang a new sign: still 'Tamsin and the Bakery,' now meaning both of them. Beat: home chosen, heart uncontained.
